# Web UI capability-gate audit

**Generated by** `scripts/audit-capability-gates.mjs`, AST-derived via the
TypeScript compiler. Run it to regenerate; it takes no arguments.

**Derived at** branch `fix/ui-capability-gates`, base `origin/develop@eef2de3`.

## Why this replaces the previous artifact

The first version of this audit was a regex over line-shaped `&&` with a
fixed 14-line lookahead. Rune found seven controls it structurally could not
see — six invoking mutating SDK methods, including Complete, Reassign and
Cancel. It also classified the *repaired* `FilesPanel` guard
(`entry.canWrite === true`) as `navigation`, because the rule named
identity/role/permission/ownership and not explicit server capability.

Both failures are worse than an incomplete sweep:

- **A stated domain the instrument cannot reach.** The limitations section was
  honest about early returns, hook-propagated props and `web-host` — and said
  nothing about ternaries or distant guards, because nobody checked the
  generator against its own description. *Naming your domain is not enough if
  the instrument doesn't cover the domain you named.*
- **A rule that erases its own findings.** Classifying the fix as
  not-a-capability-gate means a future run would not surface the instance the
  method was built to find. Every correct fix would make the method blinder.

## Counts

| | |
|---|---|
| controls (`<button>`, `<form>`, or carrying `onClick`/`onSubmit`) | **200** |
| of those, mutating (verb-based annotation, deliberately over-inclusive) | **73** |
| mutating controls with a render guard | 36 |
| mutating controls with a `disabled` expression | 40 |

Mutating controls by gate class: **CAPABILITY 21**, state 17, data 14, ungated 21.

Mutation is detected by verb rather than by an enumerated method list: the list
version missed `onJoin(c.slug)` in `ChannelBrowse`, where the component receives
its mutator as a prop. No enumeration of SDK method names can see that.

## Two properties, converging at different rates

**The candidate set is complete and verified.** 200 controls, AST-derived over
top-level `&&`, nested ternaries at any depth, and `disabled` expressions. Rune
independently reproduced the generated table byte-for-byte against the committed
one. That property is settled.

**The mutation annotation is a heuristic and will keep having gaps.** It
pattern-matches an identifier to guess whether a handler changes server state.
Making it *correct* means resolving every handler to its definition and
following it through props — real static analysis, not a better regex. Three
blind spots have been found by three readings:

| # | blind spot | found by |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | regex `&&` in a 14-line window — no ternaries, no distant controls | Rune |
| 2 | name-based enumeration — missed `onJoin` passed as a **prop** | me, second pass |
| 3 | verb needing `[A-Z_(]` after it — missed exact-name handlers `onSubmit`, `onRename` | Rune |

**(3) is the current fix.** Four rows flipped to mutating: `ChannelCreate.tsx:71`,
`ChannelSettings.tsx:202`, `NotificationDetail.tsx:688`, `ObjectiveCreate.tsx:160`.
`ChannelSettings.tsx:202` is the one that mattered — capability-guarded by
`isAdmin` and previously labelled non-mutating, so the artifact was *wrong about
a capability-gated mutation* rather than merely incomplete.

**What the annotation still cannot see**, stated rather than discovered:

- a handler whose identifier contains no state-changing verb (`doIt`, `go`, `fire`)
- a mutation reached through a wrapper whose own name is neutral
- a handler that conditionally mutates depending on runtime state
- anything requiring type resolution to distinguish a local update from a server one

**Because every control is emitted rather than filtered, a wrong annotation is a
visible error rather than an invisible omission.** Under the earlier filtering
approach `ChannelSettings.tsx:202` would simply have been absent. That is the
whole reason for annotating instead of filtering, and it is why a fourth blind
spot should land as a row someone reclassifies, not as a blocker.

## Findings

| gate | server predicate | verdict |
|---|---|---|
| `FilesPanel.tsx` Delete | `canWrite()` = admin \| owner \| objective member | **FIXED** — was `owner === viewer`, false for every namespace member |
| `ObjectiveDetail.tsx` status | assignee \| `objectives.cancel` | **FIXED** — used `members.manage`; diverged in both directions |
| `ChannelSettings.tsx` remove/leave | channel admin or self, **plus a last-admin guard** | **named, not fixed** — more permissive by construction |

The `ChannelSettings` residue is a different class from the two fixes: it does
not infer a permission from a field, and it agrees with the server about *who*.
It cannot model a condition that depends on the **state of the thing being acted
on** rather than on the actor. Fixing it needs per-action capability from the
server, which is `canWrite`-on-an-entry one level up.

## What this cannot reach

- a control gated by an early `return null` in the component body
- a gate computed in a hook and passed down as a prop
- anything in `apps/web-host`
- whether a `disabled` expression's operands are themselves capability-derived

The `CAPABILITY` rows below are classified, **not** all traced to server
predicates. Three were traced (the table above). The rest are marked by shape.
`state`/`data`/`navigation` rows were not traced at all — per the verifier's own
scoping, the point of this artifact is that the candidate set is complete before
anyone concludes which controls are non-capability.
